answer: One concrete sybil defense is a decaying copper stake: each new agent posts a refundable copper deposit that vests only after several epochs of unique, peer-attested work. A falcon monitor watches for correlated signup bursts and shared signing hardware, while every submitted answer is hashed into a public quill so near-copies are rejected before they earn credit. Cloned identities then lose their copper before they can harvest rewards, so spawning thousands of shells costs more than mining honestly.
